review_metadata.checkpoint_history_note: Root sampled_claims and SC-001 through SC-DECL-07 preserve the immutable checkpoint audit. Current delta dispositions, including resolved NPS/postal conflicts and ESI remittance treatment, are in post_checkpoint_delta and control for rolling v2.
review_metadata.method: The immutable checkpoint review remains the evidence base for unchanged material. Rolling-v2 independently inspected every added or materially changed high-risk claim, a deterministic sample of other new Verified claims, affected reusable cross-pack claims, and current machine integrity; unchanged checkpoint evidence was not re-reviewed.

pack_verdicts.rationale: Battery EPR marking and the current BIS Scheme-II route are now explicit outcome dependencies. Remaining product, port, WPC, PQMS, duty and portal uncertainties are fail-closed.
Current DGFT, ICEGATE, GST and RBI evidence supports the generic route; shipment classification, foreign-country requirements, refund entitlement and private charges remain gated.
Current substantive EPF/ESI law is supported, ESI Regulation 31's saved status was independently confirmed, and the replacement EPFO Revamped ECR page supports only the stated operational mechanics.

The stated outcome is now a portal-received frozen bid, not a valid/responsive/awarded bid. Current GeM transaction details and the bounded demo tender remain unavailable and blocked from the happy path.

New grievance and claim clocks are supported, NPS/postal threshold conflicts were correctly resolved, and the replacement live IRDAI section-39 source supports the bounded life-insurance nominee entitlement.

Urgent reporting, bank/payment-system treatment and RB-IOS escalation are bounded by current official evidence. No universal recovery promise, nationwide 24-hour completion rule or victim-authorised-transfer liability conclusion is made.

EPFO coverage now follows the current Code and the submission route remains Candidate where the portal lags. GST signature ambiguity, ICEGATE/GeM login detail and downstream consumer contracts remain gated.

findings.exact_finding: The first publication omitted the mandatory battery/battery-pack EPR registration-number marking dependency and a lot-level proof before sale release.

independent_official_evidence.locator: S.O. 4669(E), rule 10(b), Schedule I paragraph 2(ia), PDF pp.9-10
S.O. 958(E), rule 2(b), Schedule I paragraph 2(ib), PDF pp.2-3

findings.why_it_matters: A registered producer could still release a non-marked battery product, missing an outcome-critical legal condition.
findings.required_safe_treatment: Block sale release until permitted placement/method, active CPCB match, scan/readability and written CPCB notice where applicable are proved for the lot.
findings.remediation: Add a required marking task, proof, claims, sources and blocking edge.
findings.resolution_basis: The republished pack added imp.t11a, proof.battery-epr-marking and blocking edges to imp.t21; the proof checks physical/encoded number, active CPCB match, placement/method and written notice.

findings.exact_finding: The first publication did not use the operative substituted BIS Scheme II made effective on 25 February 2026.

independent_official_evidence.locator: Notification commencement p.37; Scheme II paragraphs 1-8 pp.41-44; Forms I-V pp.49-61

findings.why_it_matters: Forms, evidence, fees and licence validity were incomplete or could be routed through superseded material.
findings.required_safe_treatment: Use only the current Scheme-II forms and amounts; leave shipment-specific model/factory scope and variable testing charges gated.
findings.remediation: Replace legacy route evidence with the 2026 regulation and atomic fee/validity claims.
findings.resolution_basis: The republished task uses Forms I-IV as inputs and Form V only as the grant, with current fees and five-year validity; case-specific scope remains Candidate.

findings.exact_finding: The first publication used legacy scheduled/notified-establishment language that could exclude a non-scheduled establishment with 20 or more employees, contrary to the current Code First Schedule.

independent_official_evidence.locator: First Schedule Part I, Chapter III row; section 164(2)(b)
G.S.R. 344(E), rule 5, PDF pp.138-139

findings.why_it_matters: The old industry-schedule qualification could cause unlawful non-registration.
findings.required_safe_treatment: Treat every 20+ establishment as within the ordinary Chapter-III threshold; do not let stale portal labels narrow coverage; keep actual submission Candidate until current common Form-I is confirmed.
findings.remediation: Replace substantive coverage and registration claims with the current Code/Rules and mark old portal material Stale.
findings.resolution_basis: The republished pack does this and blocks the submission outcome on current Form-I/Form-III confirmation while keeping coverage itself Verified.

findings.exact_finding: The first publication treated 20 November 2026 as a future blanket transition checkpoint even though G.S.R. 344(E) superseded ESI Central Rules 1950 on 8 May and G.S.R. 525(E) superseded EPF Scheme 1952 on 29 June; it also carried the superseded ESI INR 21,000 ceiling.

independent_official_evidence.locator: G.S.R. 525(E), opening and paragraph 1, p.66; membership paragraph 9 pp.68-69; contribution/remittance paragraphs 18-20 pp.75-77
G.S.R. 344(E), supersession/rule 1 pp.134-135; rules 18-19 pp.159-160
S.O. 2351(E), p.2; confirms continuation after crossing a separately notified Chapter-IV ceiling but states no amount

findings.why_it_matters: Use of superseded membership, ceiling, rate or payment rules can under-enrol or miscalculate social-security duties.
findings.required_safe_treatment: Use current EPF Scheme 2026 and Social Security Rules 2026; make the unlocated current Chapter-IV ceiling and post-Code remittance rule Action Required.
findings.remediation: Replace operative sources/claims/tasks, mark old propositions Stale, and make ESI execution Candidate where current instruments are missing.
findings.resolution_basis: The republished pack adopts the current EPF and ESI rules, admits S.O. 2702(E) only for Chapter III, withholds a Chapter-IV ceiling and ESI payment deadline, and keeps the one-person non-hazardous demo outside coverage without relying on salary.

findings.exact_finding: The first publication omitted current statutory processing, deficiency and conditional interest provisions from all three EPFO death-claim tasks.

findings.why_it_matters: Claimants otherwise lack the current tracking and escalation clock and may incorrectly treat interest as automatic.
findings.required_safe_treatment: Track receipt/completeness, deficiency and payment dates; describe 12% only as conditional where the Commissioner lacks sufficient cause.
findings.remediation: Add atomic timeline/deficiency/interest claims and task tracking/escalation tied to current schemes and corrigenda.
findings.resolution_basis: The republished pack adds all nine atomic claims, exact locators and conditional wording; independent full-corrigenda review confirmed no target amendment.

findings.required_safe_treatment: Mark the old source Unavailable and claim Stale; preserve the signature conflict and use only live transaction controls.
findings.remediation: Correct access/status metadata and add a current transaction-specific claim.
findings.resolution_basis: The republished source is Unavailable, the claim Stale, the current-buttons claim is bounded, and the conflict remains fail-closed.

findings.exact_finding: The newly admitted EPFO ECR-revamp source is marked accessible, but its exact official URL redirects to epfo.gov.in and returns HTTP 404 on 2026-08-28.

findings.why_it_matters: The claim adds current regular, supplementary and revision ECR mechanics to an actionable EPF task, but the cited evidence cannot be reopened from the published record.
findings.required_safe_treatment: Replace the dead official URL with an accessible current primary source or downgrade the ECR-mechanics proposition to Candidate; do not let it establish substantive eligibility, rate or due-date rules.

Independent HTTP-200 inspection confirmed the page's September-2025-onward scope, return/payment segregation, validation, damages/interest and conditional-revision bullets plus current manual/FAQ links; the claim remains operational only.

findings.exact_finding: The first rolling-v2 publication used a 404 India Code bitstream as the sole source for a high-risk life-insurance nominee entitlement claim.

independent_official_evidence.locator: Insurance Act section 39(6)-(12), printed pp.54-55; subsection (7) on printed p.55

findings.why_it_matters: A claimant-routing entitlement cannot remain Verified when its sole published authority cannot be reopened.
findings.required_safe_treatment: Do not automate beneficial entitlement until a live current official section-39 source and its statutory qualifications are admitted.
findings.remediation: Replace the dead source and independently reverify subsection (7) with its creditor, assignment and statutory-exception boundaries.
findings.resolution_basis: The republished source now points to an accessible official IRDAI consolidation. Independent extraction confirmed section 39(7) and adjacent subsections (6)-(12); the claim remains narrowly bounded and does not generalise beyond life insurance.

unresolved_gaps.gate_assessment: All affect classification, current portal route, amount or shipment-specific approval and block dispatch/sale or post-entry closeout as applicable.
Case classification, foreign/state rules, refund eligibility and private charges are withheld from the generic happy path.
The current numeric Chapter-IV ceiling, live MCA/bank facts, state/local rules and GST case classification remain Action Required.
The pack cannot demonstrate the unavailable tender/GeM route; it stops before any claim of valid submission, responsiveness or award.
